source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: ERP vendor master record, including bank details
ERP payment run / outbound bank transfer

inputs.source: Supplier invoice uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The instruction to update the vendor record on seeing 'new bank details' in an invoice relies entirely on untrusted invoice content, with no required independent or out-of-band verification of the change.

The requirement to request approval before a payment or bank change is expressed as a natural-language instruction to the model ('request approval'), with nothing in the artifacts confirming the underlying ERP write/payment calls are hard-blocked pending approval rather than merely prompted.

'If the invoice shows new bank details' leaves to the model's judgment what qualifies as a bank-detail change; partial or disguised changes (e.g., a new remittance contact rather than a full account number) may not trigger the approval step at all.

elements.name: ERP vendor master (includes bank account details)

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model as a UI gate the clerk must click, but the clerk only sees a model-generated one-line summary; bank account numbers and change history are withheld. A more persuasive model can write a summary that omits or downplays risk (ASI09), and the ~150 cards/day volume noted in runtime notes creates approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403) that further erodes review quality.

controls.name: Raw-action approval showing full bank details and change history
controls.decay_rationale: Recommended, not present. If implemented with a true raw_action review mode, this does not decay with model capability, because the approver sees the system-of-record data directly rather than a model summary.

controls.name: Destination confirmation bound to the system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Recommended, not present. Would require out-of-band verification of any new bank destination (e.g., a callback to a phone number on file prior to the invoice, not one supplied by the invoice) before the destination can be used for payment, making the attacker-supplied bank detail unusable regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Least-privilege ERP credential scoped to the matched invoice
controls.decay_rationale: Recommended, not present. Runtime notes state the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment. Scoping it to the specific vendor/PO being processed would narrow, though not fully sever, the blast radius.

findings.title: Summary-gated irreversible payment via invoice-injected bank detail change (TC9)

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled or compromised supplier submits an invoice embedding new bank details.
Agent reads the vendor master to match the invoice to a vendor and PO.
Agent updates the vendor's bank details based solely on untrusted invoice content.
Clerk sees only a one-line model summary with no bank account number or change history, at a volume (~150 cards/day) that favors quick approval.
Agent schedules an irreversible payment that is routed to the now-updated, potentially fraudulent bank account.

forecast.watch_signal: Model/version string changes without separate review (the design states model upgrades ship with the platform with no separate review), or approval throughput/authority is widened (approvals per clerk per day rising above today's ~150, or 'approve all' / delegated-approval features introduced).

evidence.observation: Instruction says 'If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record,' acting on untrusted invoice content with no independent verification step.

evidence.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)
evidence.observation: The card shows only 'Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)' with no bank account number or indication a bank-detail change occurred.
Bank account numbers and change history are not shown to the clerk, and the clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day, consistent with consent-fatigue (SAFE-T1403).
The model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, which is the model_upgrade forecast trigger for the model_summary gate.

recommendations.action: Require raw-action approval showing the actual bank account number (old vs. new), change history, and source invoice image before any bank-detail change or payment executes; do not allow continuation on a model-generated summary alone.
Add an out-of-band verification step (e.g., a callback to a phone number on file prior to the invoice, not any number present in the invoice) before accepting any vendor bank-detail change.
Scope the ERP credential used by the agent to the minimum needed for the vendor/PO being processed, removing standing rights to update any vendor or schedule arbitrary payments.

Log and alert on bank-detail changes immediately followed by a payment to the same vendor within a short window, and monitor approval throughput per clerk (approvals/hour, decision latency) for fatigue signals.

findings.title: Unscoped ERP credential creates confused-deputy blast radius beyond the matched invoice (TC4)

attack_path.note: Untrusted invoice content is processed by the agent.
Agent resolves vendor/PO match using a credential that can read any vendor record.
Agent can write bank details for any vendor, not only the one tied to the invoice being processed, because credential_scope is broad.
The approval card does not confirm that the vendor being changed matches the vendor named on the triggering invoice.
Agent can schedule payment against any vendor record using the same broad credential.

evidence.observation: The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment, i.e., credential_scope is broad rather than least-privilege scoped to the vendor/PO on the invoice being processed.

The agent's instructions do not restrict vendor-record writes or payment scheduling to only the vendor matched on the current invoice, nor does the approval step cross-check vendor identity against the invoice.

recommendations.action: Scope the ERP integration credential to least privilege: limit it to read/write on the vendor and PO referenced by the invoice currently being processed; require a separate, more privileged workflow for anything outside that scope.
Validate that the vendor record being modified or paid matches the vendor named on the triggering invoice before executing; alert on mismatches.
As an interim, defense-in-depth measure until credential scoping ships, add a prompt/tool-level check restricting updates to only the vendor identified during invoice matching.

rating.rationale: Both findings reduce to an untrusted-invoice-to-irreversible-payment pattern (source class U, sink class S3: cap.schedule_payment is an irreversible spend, and cap.bank_update feeds it a potentially fraudulent destination), giving critical inherent risk. The only control present, ctl.clerk_approval, is structural but reviews only a model-generated one-line summary (approval_review_mode: model_summary) with no bank account number or change history shown, which under rubric section 5 step 2 credits -2 tiers to a moderate residual floor; no control severs the path (no raw-action review, no destination confirmation bound to the system of record, no credential scoping), so residual stays at the floor. Under model_upgrade and autonomy_increase triggers, the model_summary gate is expected to fail further (ASI09, consent-fatigue SAFE-T1403, consistent with the ~150 cards/day volume in runtime notes), removing the only credited control and returning the finding to its critical inherent level; forecast is therefore critical. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.clerk_approval.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in prompt.md, the approval-card artifact, and runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No ERP tool manifest, MCP/tool schema, or IaC was provided; exact API permissions behind erp.update_vendor_bank_details and erp.schedule_payment are inferred from the stable-id descriptions, so confidence on exact blast radius is medium.

Autonomy step/runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) and spawning/self-configuration capabilities are not documented; the autonomy modifier in rubric section 4 was not applied for lack of evidence, which could understate inherent risk if such limits are in fact absent.

It is not confirmed whether the approval request is enforced by a non-bypassable runtime gate or is a purely prompted behavior; the assessment conservatively assumes a structural but review-mode-limited (model_summary) gate based on the visible approval-card artifact.
